solutions.title: Hash map (one pass)
solutions.notes: O(n) time, O(n) space — interview target
solutions.description:
**Approach:** One pass with a hash map from value → index. For each `nums[i]`, look up `target - nums[i]`; if seen, return both indices.

**Why preferred:** Same correctness as nested loops, but scales. In interviews, state brute force first, then upgrade to the map.

solutions.title: Brute force nested loops
solutions.notes: O(n²) time, O(1) extra space — clear but slow
solutions.description:
**Approach:** Try every pair `(i1, i2)` with `i2 > i1` until their sum equals `target`.

**vs recommended:** Correct and easy to explain. The gap is asymptotic: the hash-map pass finds the complement in **O(1)** average instead of scanning the rest of the array. Keep this as your “first answer,” then mention the map.
